solution.name: Forever Young Solution
solution.description:
Implement a single Python script (solution.py) that reads y and l from stdin, and finds the largest base b such that y written in base b contains only decimal digits (0-9) and, when interpreted as a base-10 number, is at least l.

Algorithmic approach:
1. Base 10 is always valid (y in base 10 is y itself, which >= l). So answer >= 10.
2. For representations with k digits (k >= 3), the base b <= y^(1/(k-1)). For k=3, b <= ~10^9; for k=4, b <= ~10^6, etc. The total number of bases to check across all k>=3 is manageable (roughly O(y^(1/2)) in worst case, but practically much less since we can stop early).
3. For the 2-digit case: y = a*b + c where a in [1,9], c in [0,9]. The base-10 reinterpretation is 10*a + c, which must be >= l. We want the largest b = (y - c) / a, so iterate over valid (a, c) pairs where 10*a + c >= l, c = y mod a (or check if (y-c) is divisible by a), and b > max digit.
4. For each candidate base b, convert y to base b, verify all digits are 0-9, reinterpret as base-10 number, check >= l. Track the maximum valid b.
5. Key optimization: for k>=3, enumerate bases from y^(1/2) down to 10 (since for b > y^(1/2) we'd have at most 2 digits, handled separately). But actually for k>=3, b < y^(1/2), so we enumerate b from floor(y^(1/2)) down to 10, convert y to base b, check validity. We can also enumerate upward and break early, or just check all bases up to ~10^9 smartly.
6. Better approach: for each number of digits k from 2 upward (max ~60 for base 2), the base range is [y^(1/k), y^(1/(k-1))). For k=2 handle algebraically. For k>=3, enumerate all bases in range and check. Since we want the largest b, start from k=2 (largest bases) and work down.

Output a single integer (the largest valid base) followed by a newline.

File: solution.py
Reads from stdin, writes to stdout. Python 3.10+, standard library only.

contract.name: Forever Young Solution
contract.description: Implement a single Python script (solution.py) that reads y and l from stdin, and finds the largest base b such that y written in base b contains only decimal digits (0-9) and, when interpreted as a base-10 number, is at least l. Uses a hybrid algorithmic approach: algebraic solution for 2-digit representations, quadratic solve for 3-digit representations, enumeration for 4+ digit representations, with base 10 as a guaranteed fallback. Python 3.10+, standard library only. Reads from stdin, writes to stdout.

types.name: DigitList
types.description: A list of integer digits representing a number in some base, most significant digit first. Each element is a non-negative integer. For valid base-b representations with only decimal-compatible digits, each element is in [0, 9].

types.name: OptionalDigitList
types.description: Either a DigitList or None. None indicates that the base-b representation of the number contains at least one digit >= 10 (i.e., not representable using only decimal digits).

types.name: Phase
types.description: Enumeration of the algorithmic phases used in the solve function.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Entry point. Reads two space-separated integers y and l from stdin, calls solve(y, l), and prints the result to stdout followed by a newline. This is the top-level function invoked when the script is run.

error_cases.name: invalid_input_format
error_cases.condition: stdin does not contain exactly two space-separated integers

error_cases.name: eof_on_stdin
error_cases.condition: stdin is empty or closed before input can be read

preconditions: stdin contains exactly one line with two space-separated integers y and l
y and l satisfy problem constraints: 2 <= l <= y <= 10^18
postconditions: Exactly one integer is printed to stdout followed by a newline
The printed integer is the largest valid base b >= 10 such that y in base b has only digits 0-9 and the base-10 reinterpretation is >= l

structured_side_effects.description: Reads one line containing two space-separated integers y and l
Writes the answer (a single integer) followed by a newline

functions.name: solve
functions.description: Core solver. Finds the largest base b (b >= 10) such that y written in base b contains only digits 0-9 and, when those digits are reinterpreted as a base-10 number, the result is >= l. Implements a four-phase hybrid algorithm: Phase 1 (k=2, algebraic), Phase 2 (k=3, quadratic), Phase 3 (k>=4, enumeration), Phase 4 (fallback to base 10). Returns the maximum valid base found across all phases.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The number whose base-b representation is examined. Must satisfy 2 <= y <= 10^18.

validators.error_message: y must be between 2 and 10^18 inclusive

inputs.name: l
inputs.description: The minimum value that the base-10 reinterpretation of y's base-b representation must meet or exceed. Must satisfy 2 <= l <= y.

validators.error_message: l must be between 2 and y inclusive

error_cases.name: constraint_violation
error_cases.condition: y or l are outside the valid range (2 <= l <= y <= 10^18)

postconditions: returned value b >= 10
to_base(y, b) is not None (all digits are in [0, 9])
reinterpret_base10(to_base(y, b)) >= l
No base b' > b exists such that to_base(y, b') is not None and reinterpret_base10(to_base(y, b')) >= l

performance_budget.complexity: O(y^(1/2)) worst case across all phases; practically much faster due to algebraic shortcuts for k=2 and k=3

functions.name: to_base
functions.description: Converts the non-negative integer y into its base-b digit representation (most significant digit first). If any digit in the representation is >= 10, returns None immediately (early termination). Otherwise returns the list of digits.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The base to convert to. Must be >= 2.

postconditions: If result is not None, then result is a non-empty list of ints each in [0, 9]
If result is not None, then sum(d * b^(len(result)-1-i) for i, d in enumerate(result)) == y
If result is not None, then result[0] != 0 (no leading zeros) unless y == 0 in which case result == [0]
If result is None, then at least one digit of y in base b is >= 10

performance_budget.complexity: O(log_b(y)) — number of digits of y in base b

functions.name: reinterpret_base10
functions.description: Takes a list of digits (most significant first) and interprets them as a base-10 number. For example, [1, 2, 3] -> 123. The digits are assumed to be valid (each in [0, 9]).

inputs.name: digits
inputs.description: List of digits, most significant first. Each digit must be in [0, 9]. Must be non-empty.

validators.expression: len(digits) > 0 and all(0 <= d <= 9 for d in digits)
validators.error_message: digits must be a non-empty list with each element in [0, 9]

preconditions: All elements of digits are in [0, 9]
postconditions: returned value == sum(d * 10^(len(digits)-1-i) for i, d in enumerate(digits))
returned value >= 0

functions.name: integer_kth_root
functions.description: Computes floor(n^(1/k)) exactly using integer arithmetic. Returns the largest integer r such that r^k <= n. Uses Newton's method with integer arithmetic and careful convergence checking to avoid floating-point inaccuracies for large n (up to 10^18).

inputs.name: n
inputs.description: The non-negative integer to take the k-th root of.

postconditions: returned value r >= 0
r^k <= n

performance_budget.complexity: O(log(n) * log(log(n))) — Newton's method converges quadratically

functions.name: solve_phase1_two_digit
functions.description: Phase 1 (k=2, algebraic): Finds the largest base b >= 11 such that y in base b is a 2-digit number (y = a*b + c, with a in [1,9], c in [0,9]) and 10*a + c >= l. Iterates over all 90 possible (a, c) pairs, computes b = (y - c) / a if divisible, verifies b > max(a, c) and b >= 11, and tracks the maximum valid b. Returns the best base found, or 0 if no valid 2-digit base exists.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The number whose 2-digit base-b representation is sought.

postconditions: returned value is 0 or >= 11
If returned value b > 0: y = a*b + c for some a in [1,9], c in [0,9], and 10*a+c >= l, and b > max(a,c)
If returned value is 0: no valid 2-digit base >= 11 exists for the given y and l

performance_budget.complexity: O(90) — constant, iterates over at most 90 (a, c) pairs

functions.name: solve_phase2_three_digit
functions.description: Phase 2 (k=3, quadratic): Finds the largest base b >= 11 such that y in base b is a 3-digit number (y = a*b^2 + d*b + e, with a in [1,9], d in [0,9], e in [0,9]) and 100*a + 10*d + e >= l. For each (a, d, e) triple, solves the quadratic a*b^2 + d*b + (e - y) = 0 using the discriminant and math.isqrt for exact integer square root. Verifies b is a positive integer > max(a,d,e,10). Returns the best base found, or 0 if no valid 3-digit base exists.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The number whose 3-digit base-b representation is sought.

postconditions: returned value is 0 or >= 11
If returned value b > 0: y = a*b^2 + d*b + e for some a in [1,9], d in [0,9], e in [0,9], and 100*a+10*d+e >= l, and b > max(a,d,e)
If returned value is 0: no valid 3-digit base >= 11 exists for the given y and l

performance_budget.complexity: O(900) — constant, iterates over at most 900 (a, d, e) triples, each with O(1) quadratic solve

functions.name: solve_phase3_four_plus_digit
functions.description: Phase 3 (k>=4, enumeration): For each digit count k from 4 upward, computes the valid base range [integer_kth_root(y, k), integer_kth_root(y, k-1)] and iterates bases from high to low. For each base, converts y to base b using to_base, checks all digits are in [0,9], and verifies reinterpret_base10 >= l. Returns the best base found across all k >= 4, or 0 if none. Stops increasing k when the base range upper bound drops below 11.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The number whose k-digit (k>=4) base-b representation is sought.

postconditions: returned value is 0 or >= 11
If returned value b > 0: to_base(y, b) is not None and len(to_base(y, b)) >= 4 and reinterpret_base10(to_base(y, b)) >= l
If returned value is 0: no valid base b >= 11 produces a representation of y with 4 or more digits that are all in [0,9] with base-10 reinterpretation >= l

performance_budget.complexity: O(y^(1/3)) worst case — for k=4, base range is up to y^(1/3); higher k values contribute geometrically less

invariants: Base 10 is always a valid answer: y in base 10 is y itself, and y >= l by problem constraints, so solve(y, l) >= 10
For any valid base b, every digit of y in base b must be in [0, 9], i.e., b must be > max digit (which is at most 9), so b >= 11 or b == 10
The answer base b satisfies b >= 10 and b <= y (since y in base y+1 is just 'y' which is a single digit >= 2, and for b > y the representation is also single-digit)
For k=2 representation y = a*b + c: a >= 1 and a <= 9 and c >= 0 and c <= 9 and b > max(a, c)
For k=3 representation y = a*b^2 + d*b + e: a >= 1 and a <= 9 and d >= 0 and d <= 9 and e >= 0 and e <= 9 and b > max(a, d, e)
All intermediate arithmetic uses Python arbitrary-precision integers to avoid overflow for y up to 10^18
integer_kth_root(n, k) returns r such that r^k <= n < (r+1)^k — this is exact with no floating-point error

engineering_decisions.decision: Solution file named solution.py as implied by test harness invocation.
engineering_decisions.rationale: The test harness is invoked as 'python test_harness.py solution.py', so solution.py is the expected filename.

engineering_decisions.decision: Use a hybrid algorithmic approach: algebraic solution for 2-digit representations, enumeration for 3+ digit representations.
engineering_decisions.rationale: For y up to 10^18, bases yielding 2 digits can be very large and must be handled algebraically. For 3+ digits, base <= sqrt(y) ~ 10^9, but the number of digits grows quickly so the actual enumeration range shrinks fast. We enumerate bases from floor(sqrt(y)) down to 10 for the 3+ digit case, checking each conversion.

engineering_decisions.decision: Base 10 serves as the guaranteed minimum valid answer.
engineering_decisions.rationale: y in base 10 is y itself, all digits are 0-9, and y >= l by constraint, so a solution always exists with b=10 as a lower bound.
